family.description: This is a family of transcriptional regulators. In mammals, it activates the transcription of mitochondrially-encoded COX1 [[cite:PUB00057436]]. In bacteria, it negatively regulates the quorum-sensing response regulator by binding to its promoter region [[cite:PUB00057437]]. This entry represents the second and third domains in this protein, with one domain nested within the other.
family.name: TACO1/YebC second and third domain

causal_graphs.context: Joint protein and ATTO680-labelled mt-Co1 probe B, mouse mtDNA5446-5632; RNA100ng/ul, protein equimolar through eightfold excess,30min room temperature,10mM HEPES pH8,1mM EDTA,50mM KCl,2mM DTT,0.1mg/ml BSA,0.02% Tween20;10% PAGE in TAE.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure3A and recombinant expression/RNA EMSA Methods establish the preparation, probe B coordinates and complex formation; no isolated-domain function is inferred.

edges.mechanism: Increasing protein in the supplied probe B reaction gives a retarded RNA-containing band relative to the no-protein lane. Control mt-Atp8/6 and mt-Co2 probes lack a comparable shift under these conditions.
edges.subject: mouse-taco1-and-probeb

causal_graphs.family_mapping: NP_081622.1 exactly matches Q8K0Z7,294aa, with current PF01709 134-293. The aa27-294 His/GST fusion was expressed in E. coli ER2566 and nickel/gel-filtration purified. Tag cleavage is described for crystallization only, not this binding preparation.
causal_graphs.limitations: DIRECT denotes the joint biochemical preparation-to-complex observation. No tag-only control, absolute affinity or exclusive transcript specificity is established here. Whole mature TACO1 includes an N-terminal domain outside PF01709; binding does not by itself prove translation activation.

nodes.label: Joint mature TACO1 preparation and mt-Co1 probe B

causal_graphs.scope: Richman 2016 Figure3A, purified recombinant mouse TACO1 aa27-294, not an isolated PF01709 fragment or a mitochondrial translation reaction.
causal_graphs.title: Mature mouse TACO1 preparation forms a complex with mt-Co1 probe B

causal_graphs.context: His/GST fusion preparation, ATTO680 mt-Co1 probe B at100ng/ul, increasing equimolar-to-eightfold protein,30min room temperature in HEPES pH8/KCl/EDTA/DTT/BSA/Tween20; matched WT and mutant lanes.

evidence.explanation: Figure6C WT versus quintuple EMSA, visually checked; verified residues74-80 are outside current PF01709. The displayed probe label resolves the otherwise generic caption.

edges.mechanism: The quintuple preparation leaves substantially more free probe and less shifted RNA than WT, supporting a group-level reduction without assigning individual residue contacts.
edges.subject: nterminal-quintuple-alanine

evidence.explanation: Figure6C lower-left mutant gel versus WT and associated Results; residues112-117 are outside current PF01709, and the multi-residue effect is not decomposed.

edges.mechanism: The quadruple preparation shows a smaller binding reduction than the quintuple construct relative to WT, with more free probe retained at the displayed concentrations; not a complete binding loss.
edges.subject: nterminal-quadruple-alanine

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure6C lower-right gel and associated Results; K162/Y163/K167 fall within current PF01709 in the whole mature construct.

edges.mechanism: The triple preparation retains more free probe than WT and shows reduced binding, without establishing which residue accounts for the change or whether protein conformation contributes.
edges.subject: domain-triple-alanine

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Verified Q8K0Z7/NP_081622.1 numbering places R74/S75/R76/S79/K80 and K112/N113/K116/S117 outside current PF01709 134-293. K162/Y163/K167 are inside. All tests use the larger mature protein, not an isolated domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Each grouped substitution is one perturbation, not proof that every individual residue directly contacts RNA. DIRECT is the biochemical intervention-to-binding readout; folding, active fraction and tag contributions remain unresolved. Gels are qualitative, without fitted affinities or displayed replicate uncertainty.

causal_graphs.context: Homozygous ENU T491A/I164N, backcrossed8-10generations,30weeks, versus age/littermate-matched WT. Methods specify500ug mitochondria,150uCi35S-methionine,60min37C;50ug protein per SDS-PAGE lane and Coomassie loading check. Caption/Results mention methionine plus cysteine whereas Methods specify methionine alone.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure2D liver lanes, loading panel, caption and mitochondrial pulse Methods; isotope description discrepancy is preserved.

edges.mechanism: Mutant liver mitochondria give a weaker COXI pulse band than matched WT at equal loaded mitochondrial protein, consistent with impaired net production during the pulse.
edges.subject: homozygous-taco1-i164n

evidence.explanation: Figure2D adult-heart lanes and loading control, visually checked; do not substitute the distinct young-heart supplemental experiment.

edges.mechanism: Mutant heart mitochondria give a weaker COXI pulse band than matched WT at equal protein loading, without separately measuring initiation, elongation or nascent-chain decay rates.
edges.subject: homozygous-taco1-i164n

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Mouse Q8K0Z7/NP_081622.1 is294aa; I164 is inside current PF01709 134-293. Whole-organism point mutation and mitochondrial assays do not isolate the domain. Sequence and Results specify Ile164 despite a Leu164 typo in Figure5's caption.
causal_graphs.limitations: INDIRECT genotype-to-pulse effects do not identify a catalytic reaction, protein half-life or exact translation step. Figure2D reports three biological experiments; no mouse genetic rescue is adopted. Unchanged steady RNA abundance in Figure2B does not measure RNA stability kinetics.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure1C-D WT/KO lanes and COX1 quantification with beta-actin control; Methods define the pulse and cell context.

evidence.explanation: Figure1C-D COX3 band and WT/KO quantification, visually inspected; gene-wide perturbation rather than domain-specific loss.

edges.mechanism: The knockout gives a smaller but detectable reduction of the COX3 pulse product relative to WT; other products are not automatically assigned the same effect.

evidence.explanation: Figure1C-D reconstituted-versus-empty-vector knockout COX1 comparison; preserve the limited per-panel construct specification.

edges.mechanism: Reconstituting TACO1 raises full-length COX1 pulse signal toward WT relative to the knockout empty-vector condition.
edges.subject: human-taco1-rescue-versus-ko

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure1C-D KO/rescue COX3 comparison and reported biological-replicate statistics; no autonomous PF01709 sufficiency.

edges.mechanism: Reconstituting TACO1 restores the reduced COX3 pulse signal toward WT relative to the knockout empty-vector condition.
edges.subject: human-taco1-rescue-versus-ko

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Human reference Q9BSH4/NP_057444.2,297aa, has PF01709 136-296. CRISPR targets exon1 of the whole gene. OriGene ORF rescue is labelled TACO1, distinct from FLAG/OE conditions; complete historical clone sequence, exact lesions and per-panel promoter/tag specification remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-cell INDIRECT effects, not isolated-domain translation activity or absolute rate constants. Three biological replicates, mean/SD and two-way ANOVA/Dunnett are reported. Rescue supports gene involvement but does not assign the exact elongation microstep. COX1 RNA is not reduced, and extra pulse bands do not establish each termination position.

causal_graphs.context: RNaseI footprints from55S monosomes,25-45nt retained reads aligned to mitochondrial transcripts; codon counts normalized within transcript, sliding5-aa windows grouped by proline count, summed occupancies then normalized to WT. Cells harvested at80%confluence. Reference Q9BSH4 contains PF01709 136-296.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure2D two-Pro bars and sliding-window Methods; TableS4 and FigureS3 constrain extrapolation to individual motifs.

edges.mechanism: The two-Pro bin has elevated normalized ribosome occupancy in the knockout relative to WT, consistent with increased pausing but not itself a measured elongation-rate constant.
edges.subject: profiling-taco1-ko

evidence.explanation: Figure2D three-Pro KO/WT bars, visually inspected; Figure2C and supplementS3B provide site-profile context without independent raw-data reproduction.

edges.mechanism: The three-Pro bin is strongly elevated in knockout cells relative to WT in the normalized footprint distribution, not an absolute count of stalled ribosomes.
edges.subject: profiling-taco1-ko

evidence.explanation: Figure2D rescue/KO two-Pro bars and profiling Methods; no conversion from occupancy to a kinetic rate is made.

edges.mechanism: TACO1 reconstitution lowers the two-Pro occupancy bin toward WT compared with knockout cells, retaining the same relative-normalization definition.
edges.subject: profiling-taco1-rescue

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure2D three-Pro rescue bar remains above the WT baseline; retain incomplete restoration instead of an absolute stall-elimination claim.

edges.mechanism: Reconstitution lowers the elevated three-Pro occupancy bin relative to knockout, but does not restore the plotted value completely to WT.
edges.subject: profiling-taco1-rescue

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Whole human TACO1 exon1 knockout and ORF reconstitution, not a domain deletion. Q9BSH4/NP_057444.2 is the297-aa reference; historical clone sequence and precise per-panel rescue promoter/tag remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: INDIRECT effects on normalized footprint occupancy, not measured transit times or absolute ribosome numbers. Two prolines in five residues need not be adjacent. No displayed replicate dispersion is claimed. The three-Pro rescue remains above WT. Methods15-18nt versus Results12nt P-site offsets are unresolved; raw reads were not reprocessed. Some PP motifs do not stall and some non-Pro-rich sites do; no universal motif rule or collision-to-cleavage chain is asserted.

In bacteria, it negatively regulates the quorum-sensing response regulator by binding to its promoter region [[cite:PUB00057437]]. evidence.explanation: Mouse RNA-binding and I164N translation effects are supported, with two binding-mutation groups outside PF01709 and one inside; no isolated-domain sufficiency.
Human KO/rescue pulse products and proline-window occupancy support a translation role. Occupancy is not a kinetic constant, and neither all PP motifs nor every family member has the same effect.

discussions.prompt: Correct the mammalian interpretation while preserving imported source identity and domain boundaries.
discussions.rationale: The frozen description says mammalian TACO1 activates COX1 transcription. Inspected mouse and human experiments concern translation; the2024 profiling evidence further qualifies older initiation models. Current PF01709 covers the second/third domains, not all of mature TACO1 or historical DUF28.

evidence.explanation: The2026 human structural work and nucleotide-binding Methods motivate follow-up; its figures, commercial construct and probe controls were not fully assessed, so no new molecular transition or GTPase edge is adopted.
Bacterial YebC translation is a member-specific research lead; exact mapping, perturbation controls and figures remain to be assessed independently.
